scope: Scientific numerical intermediates for checkout-relative channel accounting. These are not new observations of human choices.

units.seller_increment: Difference in seller surplus proxy, normalized by each product listing price, per original opportunity, after seller interaction cost
units.buyer_increment: Difference in buyer surplus proxy in listing units per original opportunity after buyer interaction cost
units.joint_increment: Sum of the two participant increments; internal payments cancel but both participants' costs remain
units.conversion_increment: Expected purchase probability difference versus eligible full-price checkout, not conditional bargaining agreement
units.negotiation_rounds: Expected bargaining rounds per original opportunity, including nonparticipants as zero
units.effective_opt_in: Average stipulated participation probability; differs from base_opt_in under value-dependent odds
units.cost: Listing-price units per bargaining round, charged separately to each participant
units.monetary_interpretation: Values are normalized proxy-surplus levels, not currency profit or percentage increases over baseline

bootstrap: 2000 product-paired resamples over 193 products. Each product first averages 80 opportunities and equally averages five fixed learned-policy seeds. Intervals are conditional on simulated behavior and the fixed seed ensemble; they do not represent field or adoption uncertainty. No multiple-comparison adjustment is made, so sensitivity intervals are exploratory.

threshold_columns.value: Unclipped algebraic boundary from a ratio of average coefficients. A negative or above-one probability boundary is retained and classified, not treated as an admissible probability.
threshold_columns.maximum_cost: At the stated fallback and fixed p=.5; negative values mean no nonnegative cost gives nonnegative average increment. Exogenous boundaries are invariant to any constant p>0.
threshold_columns.both_average_participants: Minimum of seller and buyer equal-cost ceilings. This means both average increments are nonnegative, not individual Pareto improvement.
threshold_columns.joint_equal_cost: Boundary for their summed increment under equal separate costs; does not require either individual average increment to be nonnegative.
threshold_columns.minimum_fallback: Algebraic fallback boundary at c=.005. no_fallback_required means the feasible minimum is zero even when the recorded boundary is negative. A boundary above one is infeasible. Null with fallback_irrelevant status means the coefficient is zero, not missing input data.
threshold_columns.composition_crossing: Boundary under the stipulated odds rule only. Root may be outside [0,1], and ratio intervals can be unstable when the denominator crosses zero. Not an inferred adoption threshold.
threshold_columns.denominator_positive_fraction: Fraction of product-bootstrap denominator means above1e-12
threshold_columns.denominator_sign_instability: True when more than2.5% of bootstrap denominator means are positive and more than2.5% are negative. Ratio intervals are unstable across zero; retain all estimates, but do not present the point root as a reliable switching threshold.
threshold_columns.undefined_bootstrap_fraction: Fraction with denominator absolute value at most1e-12; omitted from finite ratio quantiles but explicitly retained here

files.product_coefficients.csv.gz: 48 policy-condition cohorts by193 products; low_ and high_ values are unconditional opportunity-weighted group contributions, not subgroup conditional means. low means value below listing; high means full-price checkout eligible. a_s/a_b are gross negotiation minus checkout, u_s/u_b are failed-deal checkout recovery, h is rounds, gross_s/gross_b are negotiation surplus, baseline_s/baseline_b are checkout surplus, mass is group opportunity share.
files.grid_point_estimates.csv: 2592 policy-condition-design rows covering 3 regimes by4 acceptance coefficients by4 policies by2 selection rules by3 base probabilities by3 fallback probabilities by3 costs
files.primary_intervals.csv: 960 policy-condition-selection-metric rows at p=.5,r=.5,c=.005; acceptance=.25 is the main behavioral setting
files.paired_policy_contrasts.csv: 288 paired contrasts: Full-state FQI minus each of three comparison policies, four metrics, twelve behavioral conditions and two selection mechanisms. Each interval is for the paired difference, not a subtraction of marginal interval endpoints.
files.thresholds.csv: 1344 cost and fallback boundaries with bootstrap ratio intervals
files.composition_thresholds.csv: 96 algebraic base-probability composition boundaries for seller and buyer; feasibility flags refer to point roots only
files.policy_cost_crossings.csv: 144 pairwise seller cost-crossing boundaries at p=.5,r=.5. A denominator near zero may make the ratio highly unstable; crossing flag alone is not evidence of a reliable reversal.
files.ranking_mechanisms.csv: 144 pairwise primary seller contrasts decomposed into .5 times conditional gross-surplus difference, composition adjustment, fallback adjustment and duration-cost adjustment. The common checkout baseline cancels in a comparison of policies under the same selection rule.
files.descriptive_rankings.csv: 96 rows comparing within-four-policy gross and primary seller ranks; ranks are descriptive and exclude checkout so negative channel winners must not be presented as better than checkout
files.descriptive_hindsight_loss.csv: 3240 rows: four policies plus checkout across648 contexts. Benchmark is the largest observed mean seller increment among that finite set. This is hindsight loss, not a regret guarantee or a validated selector.
files.finite_condition_summary.csv: 270 rows summarizing worst increment and maximum/mean hindsight loss across the twelve declared behavior settings for each fixed design and policy
files.summary.json: Protocol/source/manifest hashes, all input hashes, primary records and checks. primary_results and main_thresholds subset acceptance=.25 but include all three regimes.
files.accounting_tests.json: 16 fixture tests including90 bounded parameter combinations, a denominator-sign instability check and a separately labeled analytical ranking reversal
files.analysis_verification.json: Full same-environment separate-directory analysis replay, prior-rule continuity and accounting check counts
